prompt: This cast doesn't fail at compile time but causes ClassCastException at runtime. Why?
choices: Animal is not a subclass of Cat
The compiler can't always verify that a runtime cast is safe — it only checks that the types are related
Cat must override equals() for the cast to work
Animal must implement Serializable to be cast
explanation: The compiler sees Animal→Cat: these are related (Cat extends Animal), so the cast is syntactically valid. At runtime, the actual object is an Animal (not a Cat), so ClassCastException is thrown. Use instanceof before casting to guard: if (a instanceof Cat c) { c.purr(); }
